extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patentees, patent attorneys, assignees, and Patent Office officials (United States, statute dated 1836)
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory provisions governing patent application, recordation, caveats, reissue, assignments, models, extensions, remedies, and court procedure under the U.S. patent law as enacted (circa 1836). Useful for applying for, defending, assigning, reissuing, or litigating patents under this statutory regime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent fund and use of receipts
rubrics_metrics.description: Moneys received into the treasury under this act shall constitute a fund for the payment of the salaries of the officers and clerks provided for, and all other expenses of the Patent Office, to be called the patent fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies segregation of fees/receipts into a 'patent fund' to cover Patent Office expenses and salaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Succession of right on inventor's death
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person dies before a patent is granted, the right of applying for and obtaining such patent devolves on the executor or administrator in trust for the heirs-at-law (if intestate) or in trust for devisees (if testate), under the same conditions and limitations as held in deceased's lifetime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When legal representatives apply, the oath/affirmation in Section 6 shall be varied to apply to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment recording requirement and fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent and every undivided part interest is assignable by an instrument in writing and shall be recorded in the Patent Office within three months from execution; assignee or grantee pays $3 to the Commissioner for recording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordation within three months is required to have instrument entered on Patent Office records; fee is fixed at three dollars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat eligibility and filing fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Any citizen or alien (resident of U.S. one year preceding and who has sworn intent to naturalize) who has invented a new art, machine, or improvement and desires more time to mature the same may file a caveat on payment of $20.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caveat must set forth the design and purpose, principal and distinguishing characteristics, and pray protection until matured; the $20 counts toward later patent fees if a patent is obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat confidentiality and interference notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Caveats are filed in confidential archives and preserved in secrecy. If another person applies within one year for a potentially interfering patent, the Commissioner must deposit the application materials in confidential archives and mail notice to the caveat filer, who then has three months to file a full description, specification, drawings, and model to avail of the caveat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If, in the Commissioner's opinion, the specifications of claim interfere, like proceedings may be had as in interfering applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board opinions do not preclude judicial contest
rubrics_metrics.description: No opinion or decision of any board of examiners under this act shall preclude any person interested (for or against validity) from contesting the validity of any patent in any judicial court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative decisions are not binding in judicial proceedings; parties retain right to sue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue for defective/insufficient specification or over-claiming (upon inadvertence)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent is inoperative or invalid by reason of defective/insufficient description/specification or claiming more than inventor had a right to claim, and the error arose by inadvertence, accident, or mistake without fraudulent intention, the Commissioner may, upon surrender of the patent and payment of $15, issue a new patent for the same invention for the residue of the unexpired term according to the corrected specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue may be obtained by inventor or, in case of death/assignment, by his executors/administrators/assignees. The reissued patent has same legal effect as if originally filed in corrected form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annexing later improvements to an existing patent
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee desirous of adding description and specification of any new improvement invented after the date of his patent may, on payment of $15 and like proceedings as original applications, have the annexed description and specification recorded and the Commissioner shall certify time of annexation on the margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annexed specification has same legal effect as if embraced in original description; Commissioner certifies time on record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courts may award enhanced (treble) damages
rubrics_metrics.description: In actions for making, using, or selling a patented thing, courts may render judgment for any sum above the amount found by verdict as actual damages, not exceeding three times the amount, with costs, according to circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows punitive/enhanced recovery up to treble actual damages; recovery by action on the case in courts of competent jurisdiction brought by persons interested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defendant's general issue and special matter notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Defendant may plead the general issue and give the act and any special matter in evidence if notice in writing of such special matter is given to plaintiff or attorney thirty days before trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must contain the special matters intended to be proved; enables defenses based on matters set out in statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted defenses to infringement actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Defendant may prove: the specification does not contain whole truth relative to invention; contains more than necessary to produce described effect; concealment or addition intended to deceive; patentee was not original/first inventor of the thing or substantial part claimed; the invention had been described in public work anteriorly; in public use or on sale with patentee's consent before application; that patentee surreptitiously or unjustly obtained patent from another who was diligently perfecting it; or that an alien patentee failed to put the invention on sale in U.S. within 18 months of patent date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If defendant relies on prior invention/knowledge/use, he must state names and places of residence of witnesses he intends to prove possessed prior knowledge; if defenses established judgment rendered for defendant with costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court discretion when plaintiff overclaims
rubrics_metrics.description: If plaintiff's specification or claim embraces more than he was first inventor of, but defendant had used or violated any part of the invention truly and justly specified and claimed as new, court may adjudge and award costs as appear just and equitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts have flexibility to award equitable costs based on what parts were truly claimed and infringed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy for interfering patents or adverse examiner decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: When there are two interfering patents or an application refused on ground of interference, interested persons (assigns or applicants) may have remedy by bill in equity; the court may adjudge patents void in whole or part or declare rights according to priority of invention, and, if adjudication favors applicant, authorize Commissioner to issue patent upon filing copy of adjudication and complying with requisitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjudication affects only the parties and those deriving title from or under them subsequent to rendition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue and equitable relief jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: All actions, suits, controversies, and cases arising under laws granting exclusive rights to inventors shall be originally cognizable in circuit courts of the United States or district courts having circuit powers; such courts may grant injunctions according to equity principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From judgments/decrees a writ of error or appeal lies to the U.S. Supreme Court as in other cases; courts may set terms and conditions for injunctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent extension application and procedure (seven-year extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: When, after seven years, patentee desires extension beyond the term, he may apply in writing to the Commissioner, pay $40, and Commissioner shall publish notice in principal Washington newspapers and others as deemed proper of time/place for consideration so persons may appear and show cause against extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A board (Secretary of State, Commissioner, Solicitor of the Treasury) will hear evidence; patentee must furnish an oath'd statement of the ascertained value of the invention and receipts/expenditures in detail; board considers public interest and whether patentee, without neglect/fault, failed to obtain reasonable remuneration; if satisfied, Commissioner may extend patent seven years from expiration and enter certificate; benefit extends to assignees/grantees; no extension after expiration of original term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Office library appropriation
rubrics_metrics.description: A library of scientific works and periodicals (foreign and American) shall be provided for the use of the Patent Office; $1,500 appropriated for that purpose from the patent fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library purchased under direction of Committee of the Library of Congress to facilitate Patent Office duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement and public display of models
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioner shall classify and arrange models and specimens (patented or unpatented) in suitable rooms/galleries, preserve them when necessary, and keep rooms/galleries open during suitable hours for public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models and specimens should be displayed in a manner conducive to a beneficial and favorable display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-recording of pre-December 15, 1836 patents and assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons in possession or interest in patents or assignments issued/executed prior to Dec 15, 1836 may, without charge, present them to the Commissioner to be recorded anew together with descriptions, specifications of claim, and drawings; Commissioner must transcribe/copy into record books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clerks of U.S. judicial courts shall transmit authenticated copies to the Commissioner; certified copies of such records/drawings are prima facie evidence in courts without proof of loss of originals; patents/assignments not recorded anew will not be received in evidence after June 1 unless so recorded and a drawing deposited and verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue for patents lost or destroyed prior to Dec 15, 1836
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent was destroyed (e.g., by fire) or otherwise lost before Dec 15, 1836, Commissioner shall, upon application, issue a new patent for same invention bearing date of original, with certificate that it was made pursuant to act, and enter record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before issuance applicant must deposit a duplicate of original model, drawings, and descriptions verified by oath as required by Commissioner; such reissued patent and certified copies admissible as evidence and protect rights to extent original would.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner to procure duplicates of destroyed valuable models
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioner shall procure duplicates of models destroyed by fire which were most valuable/interesting and necessary for discharging duties and protecting rights; duplicates may be obtained at reasonable expense; total expenditure not to exceed $100,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A temporary board of Commissioners (Commissioner plus two presidential appointees) will determine which models to obtain and establish regulations, terms, and conditions consistent with law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for multiple reissued patents and duplicate model requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patentee desires several patents for distinct parts on reissue, he must first pay an additional $30 for each additional patent; no patent made prior to Dec 15 may be corrected and reissued until a verified duplicate of the model and drawing is deposited in the Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duplicate model and drawing must be verified by oath as required by the Commissioner before corrections/reissues are granted for pre-Dec 15 patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: No addition of improvement or new patent where original model lost (without duplicate)
rubrics_metrics.description: No addition of an improvement shall be made to any patent heretofore granted, nor any new patent for an improvement be made to the original inventor/assignee/possessor until a verified duplicate model and drawing of the thing originally invented is deposited in the Patent Office if the Commissioner requires it; similarly, no patent shall be granted where model/drawing lost until another model/drawing (if required) is deposited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compensation for such models/drawings is subject to judgment/decision of the Commissioners under limitations in section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents may be issued to assignees when assignment recorded
rubrics_metrics.description: Any patent hereafter to be issued may be made and issued to the assignee(s) of the inventor, provided assignment is first entered of record, application is made, and specification duly sworn to by the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must furnish duplicate drawings when case admits, one to be deposited in office and another annexed to patent and considered part of specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for disclaimer of overbroad claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patentee, through inadvertence, accident, or mistake, has claimed more than he was the original/first inventor of, patentee (and successors) may make a written disclaimer of such parts not claimed, attested by witnesses and recorded in Patent Office on payment of $10, stating extent of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such disclaimer becomes part of the original specification to extent of the interest possessed by disclaimant and those claiming under him; disclaimer does not affect pending actions except as relates to unreasonable neglect/delay in filing the same.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision/restriction of claims for additions and reissues
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications to add newly discovered improvements to existing patents or when patents are returned for correction/reissue shall have specifications/claims subject to revision and restriction like original applications; Commissioner will not add improvement or grant reissue until applicant enters disclaimer or alters specification/claim per Commissioner's decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant dissatisfied with Commissioner's decision has same remedy/privileges/proceedings as in original applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valid patent scope when inventor mistakenly claims others' matter (without fraud)
rubrics_metrics.description: When by mistake, accident, or inadvertence and without intent to defraud, a patentee claims as original/first inventor any material/substantial part of thing patented of which he was not first inventor, the patent shall be deemed good and valid for so much of the invention as is truly and bona fide his own, provided that part is material/substantial and definitively distinguishable from the other parts wrongly claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentee (or successors) may maintain suit for infringement of bona fide part; however, plaintiff shall not recover costs unless he had entered at the Patent Office, prior to commencement, a disclaimer to all parts claimed without right.
